.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r3/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/instruction.md (template placeholder 'CHANGE_ME: write the task prompt the agent receives.')
evidence: instruction.md reads as a recruiting lead talking to a builder, not as generated spec prose. First person singular/plural throughout: 'the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day' (instruction.md:1), 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts' (:1), 'I often move several candidates together' (:3), 'tell me who' (:3). Sentence length varies from short fragments ('Two things happen in it.' :1; 'Conversations are between our side and the candidate.' :7; 'A clear desktop workspace is what matters.' :11) to longer compound sentences. Contractions present: nobody's (:1), don't (:11, :13), it's (:13), mustn't (:13). Casual asides: 'dragging is welcome but optional' (:3), 'layout and names are yours' (:11), 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call' (:13), 'if that helps' (:13). Paragraphs are prose, not bullets; no numbered acceptance list in instruction.md. Grep over instruction.md and environment/instructions/*.md for marketing/LLM tells (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|intuitive|comprehensive|streamlin|elevate|empower|furthermore|moreover|em dash) returned no matches. Notes keep the same owner voice: hireops_rules.md:3-5 'These are the working rules for HireOps, our recruiting workspace... what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says', 'Rejected off to the side' (:43), 'Where drafts are kept is yours' (:174-175), 'What it's for' (:14). The rules file is more formal (headings, a role table, a wording table, parallel role bullets in section 6 :131-134), which is appropriate for a rules reference the brief explicitly points to and is not a voice break; integration.md is neutral operational prose, consistent with an ops note. Adversarial check: a robotic/LLM version would open 'Build a comprehensive recruiting platform that seamlessly...' with feature bullets; this brief instead opens with a question and the team's pain point. A conforming alternative (more terse brief) would also pass, so the row is not over-strict. Minor observations not rising to a defect for this row: instruction.md:13 is a dense run of runtime requirements ('It must start with..., listen on..., expose..., serve..., keep...') that reads drier than the rest, and hireops_rules.md has uneven line wrapping (:91 short wrap, :99, :112, :172-173 overlong lines) suggesting edit seams; both are formatting/structure matters for rows 1/3, not voice. No runtime evidence is required for this row; the raw evidence index was not needed.
